chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, altogether from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Hamza Al-Thumali, from Abu Abdullah (عليه السلام), who said:
Rasool-Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم) said:

Indeed, Allah took a covenant with the mu'min (believer) regarding four tribulations, the least (serious) of these being a mu'min who holds the same belief yet envies him; or a hypocrite who follows his tracks (to harm him); or a Satan who tempts him astray; or a disbeliever who witnesses his striving (against him). So what would remain of the mu'min after all of this?

key_terms.بَقَاءُ: Survival/endurance/continuity; invoked rhetorically to convey the overwhelming and incessant nature of the believer's trials
key_terms.بَلَايَا: Tribulations/calamities; plural of بَلِيَّة, referring to the divinely ordained trials that test the believer's faith and resolve
key_terms.جِهَادَهُ: His striving/struggle in the path of faith; here viewed with antagonism and opposition by the disbeliever
key_terms.مِيثَاقَ: Solemn covenant/pledge; the binding divine compact Allah has taken with every believer obligating him to patient endurance of trials
key_terms.يَحْسُدُهُ: Envies him; the act of a fellow believer harboring destructive envy toward one who shares his very creed and conviction
key_terms.يَقْفُو أَثَرَهُ: Follows his tracks; a hypocrite's act of surveilling and trailing the believer in order to cause him harm
key_terms.يُغْوِيهِ: Tempts him/leads him astray; Satan's act of seduction, deception, and incitement directed against the believer

ai.seo_question: What are the four tribulations Allah has covenanted every believer to endure, according to a hadith of Rasool-Allah (SAWW) in al-Kafi?
ai.summary: In this hadith, Imam al-Sadiq (عليه السلام) transmits the words of Rasool-Allah (صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم), revealing that Allah has taken a solemn covenant with every believer to endure four categories of tribulation: envy from a fellow believer who shares his creed, persecution by a hypocrite who trails him, temptation by Satan, and the open hostility of a disbeliever who opposes his striving in faith. The closing rhetorical question — 'So what would remain of the mu'min after this?' — is a profound expression of the relentless weight of trials the believer must bear, underscoring the centrality of patience (sabr) as a divine covenant and not merely a virtue.

en.hubeali:
A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad and Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, altogether from Ibn Mahboub, from Abu Hamza Al Sumaly, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup>

Allahazwj Took a Covenant with the Momin to exercise patience in the face of four kinds of misfortunes, the least (serious) of these is the envying of another Momin against him who has the same belief or a hypocrite who follows him (to harm him), or a Satanla tempting him, or a disbeliever showing his struggle (against him). So what would remain of the Momin after this?’
en.sarwar: 2. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Muhammad ibn Yahya from Ahmad ibn Muhammad all from ibn Mahbub from abu Hamza al- Thumali from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following:

‘Allah has made a covenant with a believer to exercise patience in the face of four kinds of misfortunes: the least serious of these is the envying of another believer against him who has the same belief, or a hypocrite that follows him (for hypocritical reason), Satan who tries to tempt him or an unbeliever against whom Jihad (working hard in the way of Allah) is necessary may cause him suffering. What then is left for a believer?”
